title: Having a hard time getting AI trading research to fact checking.
author: KeySquash6515
selftext: I'm just a retail guy, no quant background, trying to work AI into my research. Now my claude for raw financial data, gemini for news summaries, but both can sound convincing even when they're wrong. For example, I've asked for the latest stock news and gotten articles from last october instead. The info might be accurate, but it's not exactly useful if it's months out of date. So I feed results into anvita mate to compare. When they disagree, it marks in red, and I know, I must go double check. It works, sort of, still make the final call myself. How do you guys verify research? Do you have a system, or just check the key claims manually? I'd love to get it down to 10min. Looking for a better workflow.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
I’d verify claims, not whole answers. Have Claude and Gemini emit a table with claim, metric definition, period, source URL, publication date, and exact supporting passage. Then automatically reject “latest” news older than a fixed cutoff and route financial figures to primary sources first, such as SEC filings and company IR.

Your GE screenshot shows why agreement alone is insufficient: $2.20 GAAP diluted EPS versus a supplied $2.25 adjusted figure is a definition conflict, while $7.170B nine-month operating cash flow cannot validate a quarterly $2.04B FCF claim. Mark those as different metrics, not merely red disagreements. The manual pass can then focus only on stale, unsupported, or definition-mismatched rows, which is a realistic path toward ten minutes.
